always_waits.summary: Any release to main, hotfix, change to the production app, production data beyond standing read-only checks, or DNS.
Paid model runs, a paid plan or paid heavy checks, new services or accounts, or a support ticket email.
Schema or data migrations, deleting data, closing or scrapping PRs, or history rewrites.
Discards, forced cleanup, or branch deletion.
A decision that accepts a security risk: sign-in, invitations, permissions, agent confinement or admission, credentials and tokens, or CI workflow trust.
Anything on the owner's own machine or terminal window.
Upstream offers, public posts, emails, or comments on other people's repositories.
Merging past a red required check.
Firstmate self-update and restarts, or model and dispatch pins.
A decision already held for the owner; no existing hold gains a default.

may_proceed.summary: A product or design choice inside an already-filed issue, such as a copy option, a layout option, or which of two fixes.
Splitting a change and filing the remainder as an issue.
Accepting a known gap that is not security-related, with the follow-up issue filed.
An ask-user validation finding the ask-user policy escalates, when every outcome lands only on dev.
Merging a green, validated, reviewed dev PR that was waiting only for the owner's read.
The order of tickets in the night queue.
